title: T-Mem: Memory That Anticipates, Not Archives
abstract: arXiv:2606.15405v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Long-term memory is essential for conversational agents to remain coherent across extended dialogues, follow through on commitments made many sessions earlier, and adapt their behaviour to each user. Current LLM-backed long-term conversational memory, however, is reachability-bounded by the similarity between a query and stored content, both lexical and dense-vector. The approach is effective when query and memory share surface features such as wording or named entities (we call this descriptive). But it misses another, equally valuable class of cases, where query and memory do not share surface features and are tied only by a latent semantic arc (associative). On this regime prevailing long-term memory systems collectively fail. Covering this other half is what allows an assistant, for the first time, to actively draw on past dialogue as a semantic asset. translated_title: T-Mem：会预见而非仅仅归档的记忆
translated_abstract: 长期记忆对于对话智能体至关重要，它使智能体能够在长对话中保持连贯性，履行许多轮会话之前做出的承诺，并根据每个用户调整其行为。然而，当前基于LLM的长期对话记忆受到查询与存储内容之间可达性的限制，无论是词法层面还是稠密向量层面。当查询与记忆共享诸如措辞或命名实体等表面特征时（我们称之为“描述性”关联），该方法是有效的。但它错过了另一类同样有价值的情况：查询与记忆不共享任何表面特征，而仅通过潜在的语义弧线相互联系（“联想性”关联）。在这种情形下，现有的长期记忆系统会集体失效。覆盖这另一半场景，才能让助手首次主动将过去的对话作为语义资产加以利用。在记忆方面，这是认知……（摘要至此截断）
tldr: 提出T-Mem长期记忆系统，突破现有基于表面特征相似度检索的局限，使对话智能体能够通过潜在的联想性语义关联主动调用历史对话，从而预见性地而非仅归档式地利用记忆。
en_tdlr: T-Mem is a long-term conversational memory system that moves beyond similarity-based, reachability-bounded retrieval, enabling agents to recall past dialogues through latent associative semantic links—anticipating useful memories rather than merely archiving them.
